newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam to sell Maine textile mill.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam to sell Maine textile mill.

text.p: Sunbeam Corp on Thursday said it agreed to sell its Biddeford, Maine, textile mill to a group of investors including UNITE, the union that represents employees at the plant.
The investor group also includes American Capital Strategies, an investment banking firm, and a group led by Michael Liberty, a Maine businessman, Sunbeam said.
The Biddeford operation makes shells for the company's electric blankets and heated throws, Sunbeam said.
Sunbeam said it would continue to use Biddeford as a vendor and would sign a five-year supply agreement with the operation.

Management of the purchasing group will be headed by Rene Boisvert, who will serve as president of the new company. He has managed the Biddeford textile operation for Sunbeam for more than 20 years, the company said.
The purchase price was not immediately available.
A Sunbeam spokesman said the company sold the plant for $10.5 million.

The charge from the sale of the plant was included in the company's 1996 fourth-quarter results, when the entire company posted a $154.9 million restructuring charge to accommodate asset sales and other assorted costs, the spokesman said.
